evals.prompt: /git-commit I added OAuth2 login support to the auth module, please commit it
assertions: Runs git status and git diff --staged (or git diff) before drafting a message
Produces a conventional commit in the form type(scope): description
Uses feat as the type since a new feature was added
Description is in imperative mood (e.g. 'add' not 'added') and roughly 50 characters or less
Creates the commit via git commit rather than only printing the message

evals.prompt: /git-commit commit my changes: I fixed a null pointer bug in the user endpoint, updated the README, and bumped lodash
assertions: Detects that the diff mixes unrelated concerns (fix, docs, dependency bump)
Splits the work into separate commits by staging file groups individually with git add before each commit
Assigns distinct correct types across the commits (fix, docs, build or chore for the dependency bump)
Does not lump all three concerns into a single commit message

evals.prompt: /git-commit I removed the old calculate() method from the shopping cart and replaced it with computeTotal(), commit this
assertions: Identifies the removed/changed export as a breaking change from the diff
Appends ! after the type/scope in the commit header (e.g. feat(shopping-cart)!:)
Includes a BREAKING CHANGE: footer describing the migration (calculate removed, use computeTotal)
Asks for confirmation before committing given the breaking, non-trivial nature of the change
